title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: WANDA'S SHOEBOX
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wanda, a forklift driver in Klamath Falls, Oregon.
Since her mom passed, her whole family is one grumpy cat named Judge.
Then one old photo found her a family she never knew.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SHOEBOX
segments.quote: In every conceivable manner, the family is link to our past, bridge to our future.
segments.author: Alex Haley
lines: In Mom's closet, Wanda found a shoebox with one photo.
Two little girls on a porch. On the back: Me and Ruby, nineteen fifty-one.
Mom never said the name Ruby. Wanda almost closed the box.
Inside Mom's copy of Roots was a bookmark from Alex Haley:
In every conceivable manner, the family is link to our past, bridge to our future.
She kept the box open.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LIBRARY
segments.quote: Research is formalized curiosity. It is poking and prying with a purpose.
segments.author: Zora Neale Hurston
lines: At the library, Herb, a retired mailman, tapped a card from Zora Neale Hurston:
Research is formalized curiosity. It is poking and prying with a purpose.
So Wanda poked and pried through old records.
Ruby was Mom's big sister.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE WRONG NAME
segments.quote: If I have done the public any service, it is due to patient thought.
segments.author: Isaac Newton
lines: Then the trail went cold after Ruby's wedding in nineteen sixty-three.
Wanda was ready to quit. Herb slid over a card from Isaac Newton:
If I have done the public any service, it is due to patient thought.
So she slowly reread the wedding notice. The groom was Delbert Kowalski. Wrong last name!
His obituary listed his wife Ruby and daughter Tammy, in Spokane, Washington.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PHONE CALL
segments.quote: The time is always right to do what is right.
segments.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: Wanda stared at Tammy's number for three days.
She lifts two tons of lumber, but she couldn't lift that phone.
On the break room wall hung a poster of Martin Luther King Jr.:
The time is always right to do what is right.
She called at lunch. Tammy screamed so loud the forklift guys came running.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CHERRY PUNCH
segments.quote: If you cannot get rid of the family skeleton, you may as well make it dance.
segments.author: George Bernard Shaw
lines: That night, Aunt Ruby explained why the sisters stopped talking.
At Mom's wedding, Ruby spilled cherry punch on Mom's white dress. Both too proud to call. For sixty years.
Wanda thought of George Bernard Shaw:
If you cannot get rid of the family skeleton, you may as well make it dance.
So she laughed. Ruby laughed. Then Ruby said, come for Thanksgiving.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BIG TABLE
segments.quote: The happiest moments of my life have been the few which I have passed at home in the bosom of my family.
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: Wanda drove to Spokane, with Judge yelling the whole way.
On the porch: Ruby, Tammy, cousins, eleven kids, and a dog bigger than her car.
Ruby raised her glass with a line from Thomas Jefferson:
The happiest moments of my life have been the few which I have passed at home in the bosom of my family.
Wanda now has a group text with thirty-one people. Judge has not forgiven any of them.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Open the box. Poke and pry. Look again. Make the call. Laugh. Pull up a chair.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Open the box. Poke and pry. Look again. Make the call. Laugh. Pull up a chair.
I traced my own family tree once. We're mostly moustache.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
